decoded.meaning: NAME{"never"} — RFC-0014 §2 `remove-nonexistent-noop`: a removal naming a connection that does not resolve is a NO-OP SUCCESS, not an error
decoded.note: Structurally identical to `conn/remove-via-name`; only the payload string differs, and the outcome is decided by what the name resolves to at the endpoint — not by anything in these bytes. An unresolvable name (never created, or already retired) succeeds so that a retried teardown after a dropped reply is safe. `graph_t::retire()`'s own idempotence covers only an already-resolved-but-unregistered handle, so this leg belongs to the endpoint.
